findings.text: follow-on: _report_is_review swallows OSError and returns False, so a report file that exists but cannot be read — a permissions error, or a report that vanishes between the directory scan and the read — is skipped silently: it is neither listed as refused, nor counted, nor refused with a recorded store_error, which is the same class of silent drop this node set out to close.

follow-on: _delivered_report_candidates reads every candidate report twice, once in _report_is_review and again inside delivered_report_record, so the "carries no RUBRIC or FINDING line" refusal branch in delivered_report_record is unreachable from this caller and each report is read twice per pass.

item_verdicts.diff: the gained commit is b2edd1e75..27cfbda29 — it adds a _report_is_review predicate, splits _delivered_report_candidates into (candidates, refused), prints and counts refused reports, records their reason on the sidecar through plan_review._record_store_error, clears a stale reason on a committed report through _clear_store_error, and fills the evidence fragment; 3 files, 173 insertions, 26 deletions.
item_verdicts.done_when: the run's done-when for this node is the import's dry run lists refused reports, the import imports every unrecorded report, and a second pass imports zero; scripts/import_host_reviews.py _print_delivered prints "delivered reports without a record: N, refused: M" and one refused line per unbuildable report, and _import_delivered records each refusal on its sidecar and returns the refused count, so the named behaviour is delivered and the independent gate re-run at head confirms it.
item_verdicts.goal: the gained commit closes both follow-ons the earlier review of this run raised — a delivered report that is a review but whose record cannot be built is now listed as refused with its path and reason, counted separately in the per-project line, and its reason is written to its own sidecar under store_error; and the evidence fragment that was an empty anchor now records what changed, the gate and the negative controls.
item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed manifest reads complete; it names the two commits, the gate command with its result (24 passed, EXIT=0), the negative-control log and a second kept negative-control log; it names no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so no added-failure count is derivable from the reviewed run's own gate-log fields.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the gained commit changes scripts/import_host_reviews.py, tests/test_import_host_reviews.py and docs/evidence/fragments/every-review-is-kept-as-a-committed-record/delivered-reports-are-imported.html, all inside the reviewed node's declared write paths; no path outside the declaration is touched.

justifications.durability: tests/test_import_host_reviews.py:609 test_delivered_report_that_cannot_be_built_is_refused_and_recorded fails when the refusal is swallowed, so the guard the node adds is falsifiable; the stale-store_error clearing path (_clear_store_error) has no direct test, so that half is not pinned.
justifications.evidence: I re-ran the gate at head 27cfbda29 myself — 24 passed, EXIT=0 — and the kept negative-control-refusal-swallowed.log shows the new refusal test red (1 failed, 23 passed, EXIT=1); but the gate log header names rev b2edd1e75 while its 24-test result belongs to 27cfbda29 (the earlier commit's tree carries one fewer test), so a reader cannot tie the passing result to the commit it measured.
justifications.fit: the new helpers follow the module's private-helper idiom and carry no plan label, version or ticket reference, but the script reaches into plan_review._record_store_error and _clear_store_error, single-underscore helpers owned by another module, rather than through a public seam.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the two prior follow-ons are both closed at scripts/import_host_reviews.py:476-486 (a build failure is refused and listed rather than dropped), :519/529 (the reason is written to the sidecar) and in the fragment, which now states what changed, the gate and both negative controls.
justifications.reuse: the importer builds its record through the shared delivered_report_record and reuses report_carries_review_lines, _record_store_error and _clear_store_error, so the parser and the refusal writer each have one owner shared with the staging store.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches only the three declared paths of the reviewed node, and the change stays inside the node's own import script, its test file and its evidence fragment.
